rules.title: How to play
rules.intro: Avoid noise, substrates and low-FOM data. Collect Q and FOM to raise your score.
rules.powerups: Shield absorbs one hit and stacks; 3 stacked become a super shield. Double jump adds a second jump for 10s: aim for the dotted air circles for bonus points. Gold super shield breaks obstacles for 10s and scores points too.
rules.floating: Some hazards float above the ground. Stay grounded or time your jump to dodge them.

intro.title: Why λLens?
intro.abstractBody: λLens speeds up literature reviews on integrated photonic sensors. Comparing a dozen papers by hand means as many spreadsheets, copy-pastes, and transcription slips for the same FOM values (wavelength, sensitivity, Q-factor, FWHM). λLens automates PDF extraction, then visualization: from a folder of papers to an exportable chart in minutes, not days.
intro.guideBody: This guide covers both modes end to end: Mode 1 (visualization) and Mode 2 (PDF extraction).
intro.contextBody: λLens was built at Yonsei University's BPEL, within the international optics and photonics community introduced below.
intro.yonsei: Founded 1885, one of South Korea's oldest and most prestigious research universities, Seoul.
intro.bpel: BioPhotonics Engineering Laboratory, Yonsei University, directed by Prof. Donghyun Kim. Plasmonic nanostructures and structured light for super-resolution microscopy and biosensing.
intro.spie: International society for optics and photonics, founded 1955. 25,000+ members, conferences and publications.
intro.optica: Founded 1916 as the Optical Society of America (OSA), the world's leading society for light science.

mode1.title: Excel-to-Plot visualization
mode1.partIntro: The following pages walk through the Excel-to-Plot workspace step by step, from import to export.

scenario.title: Example used in this section
scenario.body: The screenshots below all come from one example: six photonic resonator sensors (silicon and silicon-nitride rings, a guided-mode resonance grating, a silicon disk on a Bragg mirror, an InP interferometer, and a polymer ring), each measured (EXP) and simulated (SIM). We compare their FOM (Sensitivity / FWHM) against resonance wavelength.

import.title: 1. Import your dataset
import.overviewBody: Once a file is loaded, the workspace has three parts: controls on the left (axes, display, filters), the chart in the middle, and a right-hand panel for comparing groups and annotating points.
import.body: Drop an Excel or CSV file onto the dropzone below, or click it to browse.
import.sampleDataLink: ↓ No data yet? Download the sample used in this guide (.csv).

import.label: Import
import.body: opens the dropzone again to load a different file.

export.label: Export
export.body: exports the filtered data as CSV/Excel, or the chart as PNG.

reset.label: Reset
reset.body: restores the default axes, display and filters, without re-importing.

import.aiNote: Columns that aren't recognized trigger an automatic AI conversion before loading. Check the result: some fields may come back missing or reworded.

controlsChart.title: 2. Chart settings
controlsChart.body: The Chart section picks what gets plotted: an optional title, then the Y and X axes. Click the section header to open it.

title.label: Chart title
title.body: optional name shown above the chart, useful before a PNG export. Auto-fills as "Y / X" until edited or cleared.

axes.label: Y-Axis / X-Axis
axes.body: either can be numeric or categorical; click a row to open a column picker. The chain icon links them (blocks picking the same column twice) or unlinks them; the ⇅ icon swaps them.

picker.label: Column picker
picker.body: Numeric and Categorical tabs, then every matching column (open here for the Y axis). Click one to plot it on this axis.

controlsDisplay.title: 3. Display settings
controlsDisplay.body: The Display section controls how the chart is drawn: scale, trend line, legend, and more. Click the section header to open it.

scale.label: Scale
scale.body: toggles the Y axis between log and linear. Log keeps widely spread values readable. Disabled if the Y axis isn't numeric.

trendLine.label: Trend line
trendLine.body: fits a curve to the points. A dropdown picks the curve type. Disabled unless both axes are numeric.

pareto.label: Pareto frontier
pareto.body: highlights the non-dominated points, better than every other point on both axes.

legend.label: Show legend
legend.body: draws the group colors on the chart itself, and is included in a PNG export.

median.label: Median line
median.body: draws a dashed line at the median value of the plotted Y axis. Disabled if the Y axis isn't numeric.

pointSize.label: Point size
pointSize.body: "Size by a measurement" scales points by a column; the slider sets the max size. Off, the same slider sets one flat size for every point.

filters.title: 4. Filters
filters.body: Filters narrow the dataset without changing the file. Each category is a dropdown: click to check or uncheck values. A summary strip always shows what's active. A category only appears if the file has that column, and "Hide needs-review" only appears if at least one row is flagged.
filters.note: Material Class and Base Materials are composite filters: a cell like "Dielectric;Semiconductor" counts toward every value it lists. The exclusion mode above decides what happens if only some listed values stay checked: Lenient (default) keeps a row if one value is checked; Strict requires all of them.

needsReview.label: Hide needs-review
needsReview.body: hides records marked "Edit", already shown with a dashed outline on the chart. Off by default.

domain.label: Domain
domain.body: classifies records as wavelength or frequency domain. By default only wavelength is kept if the file has both.

origin.label: Origin
origin.body: includes or excludes experimental (EXP) and simulated (SIM) records.

materialClass.label: Material Class
materialClass.body: filters by material category. A combined cell counts toward every category it lists.

baseMaterials.label: Base Materials
baseMaterials.body: filters by specific material (Si, Si3N4, Ta2O5...), same handling as Material Class.

exclusionMode.label: Exclusion mode
exclusionMode.body: switches between Lenient (one checked value is enough) and Strict (all must be checked).

reading.title: 5. Reading the chart
reading.body: Every point is one record. Colors follow the "Group / Color by" column, here Origin.
reading.figure4Caption: Fig. 6: FOM vs resonance wavelength, log scale, colored by Origin, sized by Sensitivity.

badges.label: Status badges
badges.body: sample count, the EXP/SIM split, and how many points are flagged for review.

legend.label: Legend
legend.body: one color per group, a static key (isolating a group is done from its card on the next page).

pointSize.label: Point size
pointSize.body: size can encode a third column: bigger means higher value. Here, Sensitivity.

median.label: Median line
median.body: dashed line at the median value of the plotted axis.

flagged.label: Dashed outline
flagged.body: flags a value the AI extraction wasn't fully confident about.

zoomControls.label: Zoom controls
zoomControls.body: lock/unlock, zoom in/out, reset. Locked by default, so an accidental scroll doesn't zoom the chart instead of the page.

hover.label: Hover
hover.body: shows the full wavelength, Q-factor and other metrics for a point.

zoom.label: Scroll / drag
zoom.body: zooms and pans once unlocked. The +/−/reset buttons do the same, reset always works.

click.label: Click
click.body: pins a point to compare it later.

rightClick.label: Right-click
rightClick.body: opens the Edit / Reset (once edited) / Pin / Hide / Delete menu, same as its Data points row.

reading.flaggedNote: A dashed outline flags a value from an AI extraction the model itself wasn't sure about. Mode 1 never validates or discards a record on its own: this outline just means nobody has reviewed it yet. That review happens in Mode 2's upcoming validation screen; doing it now is optional.

compare.title: 6. Compare groups
compare.body: The Compare groups panel summarizes the "Group / Color by" column (here Origin), with stats that always match the chart. Past a handful of groups, a search box and a "Show more" link keep the list manageable.
compare.figureCaption: Fig. 7: Compare groups panel, EXP vs SIM.

groupBySelect.label: Group / Color by
groupBySelect.body: picks the column that splits the chart (and this panel) into colored groups.

groupCard.label: Group card
groupCard.body: click to isolate that group on the chart.

groupDetails.label: Group details
groupDetails.body: mean, median and σ for this group, revealed by the chevron. The count next to the group name is always visible.

compare.note: Mean, median and σ only appear from 3 points per group: below that, a mean/median/σ wouldn't reflect a real distribution.
compare.mergeNote: Grouping by a composite column (Material Class, Base Materials) adds a "Merge multi-category points" switch, available (off by default). See it before/after in Figs. 16-17, page 18.

dataTable.title: 7. Manage your data points
dataTable.body: The Data points tab lists every record currently plotted, grouped by reference. Search, sort, and act on any point: hide it, edit it, pin it, or delete it.
dataTable.figureCaption: Fig. 8: Data points tab, R6/SIM hidden, R3/EXP and R1/SIM pinned.

filters.label: All / Visible / Hidden
filters.body: filter chips with live counts. Search and sort narrow the list further.

pinnedGroup.label: Pinned group
pinnedGroup.body: pulls every pinned point out of its normal group, so it's never lost behind a filter or a collapsed group.

addData.label: Add data
addData.body: opens the point-entry wizard covered on the next two pages.

actions.click: click a row, or its eye icon, to hide/show it. Disabled while pinned; unpin first.
actions.menu: the ⋯ menu, or right-click: Edit, Reset (once edited), Pin/Unpin, Delete (irreversible this session). Right-clicking a group's own header opens a separate menu for the whole group: pin, hide, or show only these points.

dataTable.note: Hovering a row previews that point on the chart; a hidden row previews as a faint dashed outline where it would reappear. Editing any point, manual or from a document, marks it "Edited".

addPoint1.title: 8. Add a point manually
addPoint1.body: "Add data", in the Data points tab, opens a 4-step wizard to plot your own sensor design, measured or simulated, alongside the literature. It never touches the imported file, but it does appear in exports.
addPoint1.stepperCaption: Fig. 9: step indicator. Only the current step is picked out; the others aren't a done/undone trail.
addPoint1.footerCaption: Back, Next and (step 1 only) "Save without more details" sit in a footer that stays visible across all 4 steps; on step 4 the button reads "Save" instead.
addPoint1.essentialsBody: Fill in a label and this chart's current axis values (always required, so the point can be placed), then optionally Domain, Origin, and marker shape.
addPoint1.metricsBody: Only the measurement columns this dataset actually has. Q-factor computes itself the instant Resonance Wavelength and FWHM are both filled in.

label.label: Sensor label
label.body: required. Shown in the chart tooltip and the data points list.

axes.label: Axis values
axes.body: required: the Y and X columns currently plotted. Every other field on this step is optional.

domainOrigin.label: Domain & Origin
domainOrigin.body: Origin defaults to SIM: a manually entered point is more often a design than a measurement.

shape.label: Point shape
shape.body: circle, diamond, or star. Manual points default to diamond.

metrics.label: Measurements
metrics.body: Sensitivity, FWHM, and any other numeric column this dataset has.

qFactor.label: Q-factor
qFactor.body: auto-computed as λ / FWHM once both are filled in. "Enter a different value" hands back manual control.

addPoint2.title: 9. Structure & notes
addPoint2.body: Step 3 builds the sensor's materials and layer stack. Step 4 is for optional free-text notes.
addPoint2.structureBody: Locked cascade: Base Materials, then Material Class (auto-suggested), then Layer Structure. Each unlocks once the previous node has a value.
addPoint2.finishBody: Optional free-text notes for this point.
addPoint2.converterCaption: A scratch calculator (µm/pm → nm, or µm/RIU → nm/RIU) for converting a paper's value by hand.

baseMaterials.label: Base Materials
baseMaterials.body: search or add a value: what this point is physically made of.

materialClass.label: Material Class
materialClass.body: pre-checked from what this dataset pairs with those materials. Edit it by hand and the auto-suggestion stops.

layerStructure.label: Layer Structure
layerStructure.body: pick each layer's material, drag to reorder, set a thickness in nm, and a repeat count for periodic stacks. A live preview updates as you go.

addPoint3.title: 10. The result on the chart
addPoint3.body: Once saved, the point appears on the chart immediately: a gold-outlined diamond with a brief pulse ring where it lands.
addPoint3.figureCaption: Fig. 13: the new point on the chart, marked and counted separately.

manualCount.label: Added manually
manualCount.body: counts points added by hand, separately from the file's own samples.

newPoint.label: The new point
newPoint.body: a gold-outlined diamond, with a brief pulse ring right after it's added to help you spot it on the cloud.

addPoint3.note: A toggle in the Data points tab decides whether manual points count toward the median, trend line and Pareto frontier.

annotate.title: 11. Pin and annotate
annotate.body: Clicking a chart point pins it here as a card, a lightweight session-only bookmark for comparing specific records. Click a card's header to expand it.

sort.label: Sort
sort.body: orders pinned cards by date added or by reference.

showOnlyPinned.label: Show only pinned points
showOnlyPinned.body: narrows the chart and the Compare groups panel down to pinned rows.

compareSelect.label: Compare selection
compareSelect.body: check a card, or use Select all / Deselect all. Pinning a card auto-selects it too, up to 6, then "Compare (N)" opens a side-by-side comparison view.

card.label: Pinned card
card.body: reference, title and plotted axis values. Click to expand.

siblings.label: Pin this paper's other rows
siblings.body: shown while any of the paper's other records remain unpinned; one click pins them all.

layerStructure.label: Layer Structure
layerStructure.body: a visual layer stack with thicknesses. The zoom icon opens a larger, exportable PNG view.

metrics.label: Metrics
metrics.body: measurements not already in the header. Same zoom-to-PNG shortcut as Layer Structure.

notes.label: Notes
notes.body: an editable note, pre-filled from the Notes/Evidence columns when available.

comparePins.title: 12. Comparing pinned points
comparePins.body: Selecting 2 or more pinned cards (up to 6) enables the "Compare (N)" button, opening a view with the points side by side. The title pre-fills from the pinned references and stays editable.
comparePins.figureCaption: Fig. 15: comparing the two points pinned on page 16.

sections.origin: whether the record is measured (EXP) or simulated (SIM).
sections.mode: the Mode ID and, when present, its description.
sections.structure: Material Class, Base Materials, and the layer stack.
sections.metrics: every plotted or recorded numeric value.
sections.notes: the free-text note attached to the pin.

comparePins.note: Zoom (bottom right), dragging the ⇄ handle above a column to swap it with another, and clicking the title to rename it round out the preview. "Download comparison PNG" exports the result as a PNG.
comparePins.markupBody: Before exporting, freely annotate the preview: drawing, frames, arrows, underlines and sticky notes, each in a color of your choice, plus fixed-color stamps.

tools.label: Toolbar
tools.body: selection, pan, pen (with color), highlight a row, frame, arrow, underline, sticky note, eraser; favorite/validated/exclude stamps; undo/redo.

clear.label: Reset annotations
clear.body: removes every stroke, shape and sticky note. Keeps the title and section choices.

manage.label: Compared points
manage.body: drag a chip to reorder it, × removes it (up to 6); sort them and pick which sections show, or highlight the best/worst, via "Display settings".

exportChart.title: 13. Exporting the chart
exportChart.body: The filtered dataset exports as a spreadsheet, and the chart as configured exports as an image.
exportChart.chartCaption: Fig. 16: grouped by Material Class, merge on.
exportChart.chartCaption2: Fig. 17: grouped by Base Materials, merge off.
exportChart.mergeExplain: "Merge multi-category points" applies to any composite column, switching on automatically the moment you group by one. On (left), a multi-category record collapses into one multi-color marker. Off (right), it plots once per token, each with its own color.

formats.csv: the filtered rows as a CSV file.
formats.xlsx: the filtered rows as an Excel workbook.
formats.png: the chart as displayed, with title, legend and any overlay, as a PNG image.

exportPin.title: 14. Exporting a pinned point
exportPin.body: A pinned point's details also export on their own, at three levels: everything in one image, or just its layer structure.
exportPin.pinExportCaption: Fig. 18: every field combined into one PNG.
exportPin.metricsExportCaption: Fig. 19: numeric measurements only, no structure or notes.
exportPin.layerOrderNote: Layers are listed top to bottom as written in the file: the first is whichever material light reaches first, not necessarily the thickest. This preserves the paper's own physical order.

pinFormats.note: the note text, as its own .txt file.
pinFormats.fields: the Metrics box (or Layer Structure) as a small standalone PNG.
pinFormats.all: everything on the card (Origin, Mode, structure, metrics, note) as one PNG.

mode2Drop.title: 1. Drop your PDFs
mode2Drop.body: Drop up to 10 PDF papers and pick which Gemini model analyzes them.

files.label: Staged files
files.body: Page count, size and a rough time estimate. Drag a card to reorder the batch.

model.label: Model
model.body: Default tries the strongest model first. It falls back automatically if the quota runs out.

launch.label: Launch
launch.body: Starts the batch (files aren't uploaded until now, not when dropped). Stays disabled until at least one file is staged.

mode2Running.title: 2. Follow the extraction
mode2Running.body: Files process one at a time. The header tracks overall progress and the journal logs every event.

header.label: Progress
header.body: Overall progress and a rough time remaining, refreshed every second. Hovering a file icon in the strip below shows its name and status.

notice.label: Quota notice
notice.body: Gemini's free quota can run out mid-batch. The held file retries automatically and nothing is lost.

files.label: Current & next file
files.body: The file currently being handled, and the one queued next.

log.label: Journal
log.body: A timestamped log of every file starting, finishing, or waiting for retry.

game.label: Docked minigame / PDF preview
game.body: Photon Dash starts folded, right here (a quiet gamepad icon in the app's own footer opens the same game separately, any time, outside of a run). While folded, this spot instead shows a live preview of whichever file is currently being analyzed.

mode2Review.title: 3. Review a record
mode2Review.body: Once extraction finishes, every proposed value is listed with its source paper. A row the model isn't sure about is flagged for a second look.
mode2Review.pdfCaption: Simplified stand-in. The real viewer shows your PDF page with the cited passage highlighted automatically.
mode2Review.note: There's no forced "done" state here: a "Continue to export" button moves on whenever you're ready, whether or not every flagged row has been checked. A short summary screen between Running and Review recaps how many records need a look.

table.label: Rows & tabs
table.body: Filter by All, To confirm, or Excluded. Click a row to inspect it.

callout.label: Evidence
callout.body: The exact quote the model cites, and where it found it. Click a location to jump the viewer there.

actions.label: Decide
actions.body: Approve, correct, or exclude the selected row, then move to the next one.

pdf.label: Source page
pdf.body: The cited page for the selected row, auto-scrolled to the passage.

mode2Correct.title: Correcting a flagged record
mode2Correct.body: Every field on the card is corrected in place: click its pencil, edit the value, then confirm with Enter (or the ✓ icon); Escape (or ✕) cancels. No separate form to open. This doesn't advance the stepper above: correcting is part of the Review step, not a stage of its own.
mode2Correct.note: Only some fields can be edited by hand. Evidence, Location, Review status, Raw Value and Conversion Method stay machine authored.

banner.label: Flag reason
banner.body: Shown right at the top of the card the moment a record needs review or is excluded, with nothing to open.

sources.label: Sources
sources.body: One click jumps straight to the matching quote in the PDF.

pencil.label: Edit a field
pencil.body: Every field has its own pencil: click, edit the value, confirm with Enter.

mode2Export.title: 4. Export your data
mode2Export.body: A last preview before saving. Excluded rows stay visible, struck through, for traceability.
mode2Export.note: Reviewed by shows AI until a human validates, corrects or excludes a row. Then it records who and when.

legend.label: Preview count
legend.body: How many rows will be in the export in total, and what the grayed out rows below mean.

table.label: Preview
table.body: Every extracted row, including excluded ones, exactly as it will be exported. Q-factor isn't part of this export; Reviewed by (AI, or who and when a human reviewed it) is.

save.label: Ready to save
save.body: How many rows are ready, excluded, and confirmed. Name the file, pick .xlsx or .csv, and save it.

mode2.title: PDF extraction & validation
mode2.partIntro: The following pages walk through PDF extraction step by step, from your first drop to a validated export.

about.body: This guide was designed and built by Danaé Albrecht-Martin, a software engineering intern (apprentice at CNAM Grand Est) from July 6 to September 6, 2026, at Yonsei University's BPEL. Her role spanned all of λLens: application architecture, the PDF extraction pipeline, and the interactive visualization interface.
about.supervision: Supervised by Professor Donghyun Kim (Yonsei University, School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering; Fellow of SPIE/Optica, Senior Member IEEE, President of the OSK), and Inseop (BPEL).

controls.title: Chart Title
controls.axisLinkedHint: Linked: prevents X and Y from sharing the same axis
controls.axisUnlinkedHint: Independent: X and Y may share the same axis
controls.trendLineHint: Requires numeric X and Y axes

fomcharts.paretoExplain: Connects the non-dominated points: no other point is better on both X and Y.
fomcharts.pointSizeLegendExplain: The larger the point, the higher its {column} value.
fomcharts.manualHint: Diamond markers with a gold outline are points you added manually. They aren't from a document.
fomcharts.missingAxisHint: These rows have no value for the selected X or Y axis, so they can't be placed on the chart. Pick a different axis to see them.

workspace.title: Analysis workspace
workspace.pinHint: Click a point to pin an annotation

stats.title: Compare groups

tooltips.n: Count of points from this group plotted on the chart.
tooltips.mean: Average of the plotted Y-axis values for this group.
tooltips.median: Middle plotted Y-axis value for this group. Matches the dashed median line when this group is isolated.
tooltips.std: Standard deviation of this group's plotted Y-axis values: how spread out they are around the mean.

stats.isolate: Isolate this group on the chart (doesn't affect the stats)

annotations.title: Annotations
annotations.empty: No pins yet. Click any point on the chart to bookmark it.
annotations.showOnlyPinnedTooltip: Hides every point except the ones pinned below. Stats narrow down to this same selection too.
annotations.pinSiblings: + Pin {count} other point | + Pin {count} other points

compare.title: Compare pinned points
compare.description: Pick which sections to include and, optionally, a title for this image.
compare.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Ring resonators vs. grating sensors

chips.hint: Drag a chip, or use the arrows, to reorder columns live. Remove a point with × without closing this dialog.

tools.pointerHint: Click any annotation to select it, drag to move it, then use the × that appears or press Delete to remove it.
tools.panHint: Drag to scroll around the preview. Tip: hold Space with any other tool to pan temporarily.
tools.penHint: Draw freely over the preview to highlight or circle a detail.
tools.eraserHint: Drag over one or more annotations to erase them.
tools.highlightRowHint: Click a row to highlight it across every column.
tools.frameHint: Drag over a value to circle it.
tools.arrowHint: Drag to draw an arrow pointing at a detail.
tools.underlineHint: Drag under a detail to underline it.
tools.postitHint: Click to drop a note and type your text. Drag it to move it, double-click to edit it again.
tools.stampHint: Click anywhere on a column to stamp it with the selected mark.

compare.empty: Pick at least one section to include.

addPoint.title: Add a data point
addPoint.description: Compare your own sensor against the literature. It isn't saved to the file, but it does appear in exports.
addPoint.editDescription: Change any value below. The original values stay recoverable with "Reset this point", separate from the toolbar's general "Reset".
addPoint.noStructureFields: This dataset has no structure/material columns to fill in.
addPoint.noMetricFields: This dataset has no extra metric columns to fill in.
addPoint.modeIdHint: Optional. Leave blank if not relevant.
addPoint.noBaseMaterialsYet: Add a Base Material above first. A layer can only be made of a material already listed there.
addPoint.structureIntro: Base Materials → Material Class → Layer Structure: each level unlocks once the previous one has a value.
addPoint.materialClassSuggestedHint: Suggested from the materials you picked. Check the box(es) that apply, or adjust them.
addPoint.alreadyEditedHint: This point was already edited. Saving now updates it again. "Reset this point" (in Data points) always restores the original values.
addPoint.qFactorHint: Q-factor measures how sharp the resonance is: Q = λ / FWHM. Not stated directly? Compute it from those two values.

converter.title: Unit converter
converter.hint: Every field here is in its canonical unit (nm / nm/RIU). Convert here, then copy the result or insert it directly into the matching field.

addPoint.layerRepeatHint: How many times this layer (or period, with the rows next to it) repeats. E.g. 10 for a 10x Bragg mirror period. Leave blank otherwise.
addPoint.notesPlaceholder: Any extra context worth remembering about this point...
addPoint.provenanceHint: This point is added manually, not sourced from a document. It's marked as such everywhere: chart, table, exports.
addPoint.includeInStats: Include my added points in statistics
addPoint.includeInStatsHint: When off, your added points still appear on the chart, but are excluded from the median, trend line, Pareto frontier, and sample count.

pointsTable.title: Data points
pointsTable.deleteConfirm: Permanently delete this point? Can't be undone this session (re-import the file to get it back).
pointsTable.pinnedHint: Stays here even when hidden from the chart. A pinned point is never lost.
pointsTable.pinGuardHint: Unpin first to hide or delete

tooltips.groupBy: Colors points by this column so you can compare groups at a glance.
tooltips.scale: Log keeps values that span several orders of magnitude readable. Linear keeps equal spacing between values.
tooltips.legend: Draws the legend on the chart itself, so it's included when exporting as an image.
tooltips.median: Draws a dashed line at the median Y value of the points plotted.
tooltips.trendLine: Fits a curve through the points to show the overall trend. Needs numeric X and Y axes; "Auto" picks whichever shape fits best.
tooltips.trendType: The mathematical model the trend line fits (linear, exponential, logarithmic, power, or polynomial). "Auto" keeps whichever has the highest R².
tooltips.pareto: Highlights the non-dominated points, not beaten on both axes by any other point.
tooltips.trendUnavailable: Needs at least 2 points with different X values to draw anything.
tooltips.exclusionMode: Strict excludes a point as soon as it contains one unchecked material/class. Lenient only excludes it once ALL of its materials/classes are unchecked.
tooltips.mergeMultiCategory: A multi-category point normally plots once per category. Turn this on to show a single gradient marker instead.
tooltips.excludeNeedsReview: Hides points whose Review status is "Edit" (the dashed outline on the chart).
tooltips.pointSizeMode: Turn on to size each point by a chosen measurement; off for one flat size everywhere.
tooltips.pointSizeBy: The measurement that drives point size while "Size by a measurement" is on.
tooltips.pointSize: Point size: the maximum size in "by measurement" mode, or the single flat size in constant mode.
